intro: The simple future: what you think will happen later.
p.vendré.consejo: «Venir» loses its i in the future: «vendré», not «veniré». The é has an accent.
p.vendrás.consejo: For «tú» the ending is -ás: «vendrás». The accent shows where the stress falls.
p.vendrá.glosa: he, she or you (usted) will come
p.vendrá.consejo: With the accent, «vendrá» is the future. «Vendra» without it does not exist in Spanish.
p.llegará.glosa: he, she or it will arrive
p.llegará.consejo: Regular verb: whole infinitive plus -á: «llegar» + «á» = «llegará». The ll sounds y.
p.hablaré.consejo: «Hablaré» (future) is not «hablé» (past). The future keeps the -r of the infinitive.
p.tendré.consejo: «Tener» changes its stem: «tendré», not «teneré». A new d appears in the middle.
p.haré.glosa: I will do, I will make
p.haré.consejo: «Hacer» loses «ce» in the future: «haré», «harás», «hará». The h is silent.
p.saldré.glosa: I will leave, I will go out
p.saldré.consejo: «Salir» adds a d: «saldré», «saldrás». It is irregular, like «venir» and «tener».
p.podré.consejo: «Poder» loses its e: «podré», not «poderé». An infinitive follows: «podré venir».
p.creo que.consejo: «Creo que» + future is an opinion about later: «creo que lloverá».
p.mañana.consejo: It sounds very natural with the future: «Mañana hablaré con ella».
p.tarde.consejo: As an adverb it does not change: «llega tarde». As a noun, «la tarde» is the part of the day.
p.por la tarde.consejo: For an exact time you use «a las seis». For the part of the day, «por la tarde».
p.el tren.consejo: It is masculine: «el tren», «un tren». You travel «en tren», with no article.
b1.texto:
You add the ending to the **whole infinitive**: **-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án**.

- hablar**é**, comer**é**, vivir**é**
- llegar**á**, vendr**á**

Some verbs change the stem: **vendré, tendré, haré, saldré, podré, diré**.

**Creo que** + future is an opinion about later: creo que el tren **llegará** tarde.
b2.f0.texto: I think the train will arrive late.
b2.f3.texto: Then I'll have time at six.
b2.f4.texto: Tomorrow I'll talk with your sister.
b2.f5.texto: She'll leave the house at seven.
b2.f7.texto: Then I'll be able to eat with you.
b4.titulo: The six endings of the future
b4.texto:
With **hablar**:

- yo hablar**é**
- tú hablar**ás**
- he, she, usted hablar**á**
- we hablar**emos**
- you plural (vosotros) hablar**éis**
- they, ustedes hablar**án**

The endings are the same for **-ar, -er and -ir** verbs. Some verbs change the stem, and the most useful are **tener** (**tendré**), **venir** (**vendré**), **hacer** (**haré**), **salir** (**saldré**), **poder** (**podré**) and **decir** (**diré**).
b4.e0.texto: Tomorrow I will talk with Ana.
b4.e1.texto: I think Pablo will come late.
b5.f0.texto: The train will arrive with the last light of the afternoon.
b5.f1.texto: Its wheels will sing a slow song on the cold iron.
b5.f2.texto: The white smoke will rise slowly toward the clouds.
b5.f3.texto: The doors will open with a metallic sigh.
b5.f4.texto: I will wait on the platform with cold hands.
b5.f5.texto: My sister will step out first with a red suitcase.
b5.f6.texto: Her green coat will shine under the yellow lamps.
b5.f7.texto: We will walk together along the wet street.
b5.f8.texto: The air will smell of rain and toasted bread.
b5.f9.texto: The hot soup will warm our hands.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That gives «hablé», which is past. The future removes nothing.
b6.o2.refuerzo: In Spanish the endings always go at the end.
b6.pregunta: Where is the future ending added?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: a prediction uses the future.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Llega» is the present: a timetable or a habit.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Llegó» is the past: it has already happened.
b8.frase: Creo que el tren llegará tarde
b8.traduccion: I think the train will arrive late
b9.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Venir» changes its stem: vendr-.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Venir» is irregular and loses its i: vendr-.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Vengo» is the present, not the future.
b9.pregunta: What is the future of «venir» with «yo»?
b10.o0.refuerzo: The stem of «tener» changes: tendr-, not tener-.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Correct: stem tendr- plus the ending -é.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Tengo» is the present; here you talk about six o'clock, later on.
b10.pregunta: Which form of «tener» goes with «yo» in the future?
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Vendrás» is tú: that would speak about the other person.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Vendrá» is él or ella, not you or me.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Perfect! You talk about yourself, so «vendré».
b12.pregunta: You are asked: «¿Vendrás mañana?». You will go in the afternoon. What do you say?
p.saldrá.consejo: «Salir» adds a d in the future: «saldré», «saldrá». The accent marks the final stress.
p.saldremos.consejo: It comes from «salir»: stem «saldr-» plus -emos. It is the future of «nosotros».
p.ruedas.consejo: It is the plural of «rueda». The initial r sounds strong, like rr.
p.cantarán.consejo: The whole infinitive «cantar» plus -án. The accent marks the last syllable.
p.lenta.consejo: It agrees with the noun: «canción lenta», «tren lento».
p.humo.consejo: The h is silent: U-mo. It is masculine: «el humo».
p.subirá.consejo: The infinitive «subir» stays whole in the future, and -á is added. The v sounds b.
p.abrirán.consejo: The participle «abierto» is irregular, but the future «abrirán» is regular: infinitive plus -án.
p.suspiro.consejo: It comes from «suspirar». It is masculine: «un suspiro».
p.esperaré.consejo: «Esperar» also means «to hope»; the context shows which one. The accent marks the final stress.
p.brillará.consejo: The ll sounds like y: bri-ya-RA. It is a regular verb: infinitive plus -á.
p.lámparas.consejo: The accent shows the stress on the first syllable: LAM-pa-ras. It is the plural of «lámpara».
p.caminaremos.consejo: The whole infinitive «caminar» plus -emos. The stress falls on «re».
p.olerá.consejo: «Oler» changes in the present («huele»), but the future «olerá» is regular. It is followed by «a»: «olerá a pan».
p.calentará.consejo: «Calentar» changes e to ie in the present («calienta»), but not in the future: «calentará».
p.infinitivo.consejo: It is the form that ends in -ar, -er or -ir: hablar, comer, vivir. The v sounds b.
p.entero.consejo: It agrees with the noun: «el infinitivo entero», «la semana entera».
p.é.consejo: The accent shows the final stress: «hablaré». Without it, «hable» is another form.
